title: Open book. Your index is your score, not your memory.
lede: Nobody passes the Florida UE exam by memorizing the code. It's open book, and every question is worth the same. You pass by finding the answer fast, about 3 minutes a question, 75% to clear. The one thing that separates people who pass from people who run out of time is how well their books are tabbed and indexed. That's the skill this app drills.

moves.title: Get the books
moves.body: The exact approved reference list, no more and no less. Ordering the wrong edition, or a book that isn't on the list, is a quiet way to fail before you start.

moves.title: Tab & index them
moves.body: The biggest lever, and where most people under-invest. Permanent tabs, a marked-up index, and knowing each book cold so your hand goes to the right page without thinking.
moves.where: kit · compartment C, then the Book Map

moves.title: Drill the lookup til it's a reflex
moves.body: Noun, tab, table, footnote, in that order. Fast, every time. Practice the path until finding an answer is muscle memory, not a hunt.

mythBuster: It's not a closed-book memory test. Field experience helps you understand the question, but it won't find the answer for you. Speed in your books will. The people who struggle are almost always the ones whose books aren't tabbed.
examShape: 75% to pass, every question equal weight
Permanent tabs only. No sticky notes, loose sheets, or formula pages
One original copy of each required reference

cib.label: Read the Candidate Information Booklet (CIB)
cib.note: the official source of truth. Confirm your book list, editions, and exam-day rules here before anything else.

freePractice.label: Practice on the real code for free
freePractice.body: You don't need to buy a thing to start building the lookup habit. NFPA puts the NEC (NFPA 70), 2023 edition, online as free read-only access through NFPA LiNK. A free account signs you in. Open it, work the index, and practice finding sections cold before your own tabbed copies arrive.

steps.heading: Where the rules actually come from
steps.body: Florida's DBPR Electrical Contractors page and the Candidate Information Booklet (CIB) are the source of truth for the approved reference list, editions, and exam-day rules. Confirm you're tracking the Unlimited Electrical (UE) license, and treat the CIB as final, not this app and not a forum.

steps.heading: Two parts, Technical first
steps.body: The UE exam has a Technical part (100 questions, 5 hours) and a separate Business part (50 questions, 2.5 hours). This app is Technical first. Wiring, protection, OSHA and safety, and alarms sit closest to daily trade work, so clearing Technical first builds momentum and proves out your reference-book setup. The Business kit is a post-beta stub (sidebar compartment F, unlocked past the halfway mark).

steps.heading: Exam-day bring rules
steps.body: One original copy of each required reference, with permanently attached tabs only. No sticky notes, no removable flags, no loose notes or formula sheets in the room. Confirm the exact list against your CIB before exam day (sidebar compartment D).

steps.heading: Edition pins
steps.body: This beta is pinned to NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023 edition and OSHA Title 29 Parts 1926, 1910, and 1904, July 2020 edition. Both are scheduled to flip on 2027-08-21. Always verify the current CIB-approved edition before you buy. This app never substitutes for your book.
